label: Work and Burnout
framing: Burnout is not always a sign you are doing too little. Often it is the sign of a body and soul kept under load that God never asked you to carry, with no rhythm to set it down. Scripture treats your labor as good and your limits as built in, not as flaws to be overcome.
cultural: Most people in the biblical world worked the land or a trade from dawn to dark, and the threat was never idleness but a master, a debt, or a harvest that demanded everything. Into that grind God wrote a weekly stop into the law itself, and called it freedom, since only a slave is denied rest. Even Israel's fields were given a year off.
historical: The monastic rule of Benedict in the sixth century ordered the day into work, prayer, and rest so that no one part swallowed the others, and the church carried that balance for a thousand years. The Reformers later raised ordinary work to a calling, though their heirs sometimes turned that gift into the engine of a relentless striving the Sabbath was meant to break.
application: Treat your limits as a message, not an enemy, and ask what the exhaustion is trying to tell you. Build a real stop into your week and defend it before the work eats it. Refuse the lie that your worth rises and falls with your output. And if the burnout has hollowed out your sleep, your joy, and your love for the people closest to you, get help, because that is not weakness but stewardship of the one body you were given.

verses.text: Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
Six days you shall do your work, but on the seventh day you shall rest.
It is in vain that you rise up early and go late to rest, for he gives to his beloved sleep.
Come away by yourselves to a desolate place and rest a while.
Better is a handful of quietness than two hands full of toil and a striving after wind.

articles.label: Practical guides for work and money

label: Calling and Purpose
framing: Calling is wider than a career and deeper than a job you happen to like. Scripture roots it first in whose you are before what you do, and it dignifies the ordinary work of hands and home as a place where God is served. You do not have to find one perfect role to live a life that matters.
cultural: In the ancient world a person's work was usually fixed at birth by family and station, and the idea of choosing a path was nearly unknown. Paul told slaves and free, weavers and fishermen, to serve the Lord in the place they stood, which meant the dishwasher and the deacon shared the same dignity, and the work of the hands was never beneath the work of the spirit.
historical: For centuries the church reserved the word calling for priests and monks, until the Reformers of the sixteenth century returned it to the farmer, the mother, and the magistrate, insisting that God is served at the plow as truly as at the altar. The Puritans then taught that a faithful life is built less of grand destiny than of daily duty done well before God.
application: Start not with what is unique about you but with who is in front of you, since calling usually meets you in your obligations before it meets you in your dreams. Do the work you have well, as unto God, and let the larger shape clarify over years rather than in a flash. Watch where your gifts and the world's real needs overlap. And measure a life not by its title but by its love.

verses.text: Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men.
Whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
We are his workmanship, created for good works, which God prepared beforehand.
Let each person lead the life that the Lord has assigned to him.
What does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God.

articles.label: Practical guides for work and money

label: Decisions and Guidance
framing: God's guidance is more often a settled character than a secret map. Scripture promises wisdom to those who ask and a light for the next step, not a blueprint of the whole road. The aim is not to crack a code but to become the kind of person who chooses well.
cultural: Israel's neighbors read the future in entrails, stars, and omens, desperate to wrest the will of the gods from a silent sky. Against all of it, God gave his people his word, his wisdom, and his Spirit, and forbade the divination that treated guidance as a trick to be worked rather than a relationship to be lived.
historical: The desert fathers of the fourth century practiced discernment as the testing of inner movements before a wise elder, never alone. Ignatius of Loyola in the sixteenth century gave the church careful rules for weighing the desires of the heart against the consolations and disturbances they bring, and the broad tradition has always set Scripture, counsel, providence, and a peace that endures alongside one another.
application: Ask God plainly for wisdom, then do the unglamorous work that wisdom requires: read the Scriptures, seek counsel from people who know you and will tell you the truth, and weigh the real costs honestly. Where the Bible is silent, you are freer than you fear, so move toward what builds love and away from what feeds the self. Make the decision, then keep walking, trusting that a misstep made in faith is not beyond God to redirect.

verses.text: If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all.
Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and he will make straight your paths.
Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
In an abundance of counselors there is safety.
The heart of man plans his way, but the Lord establishes his steps.

articles.label: Practical guides for the inner life

label: Rest and Sabbath
framing: Rest is not the reward for finishing your work. It is a command, given by a God who rested when nothing forced him to, and a weekly declaration that the world holds together without you. To keep a Sabbath is to confess that you are not God, and to be glad of it.
cultural: No nation around Israel rested a day in seven, and to a watching empire a people who stopped every week looked like fools throwing away a seventh of their labor. But the command was rooted in the deepest places, in God's own rest at creation and in Israel's deliverance from a Pharaoh who never let slaves stop. To rest was to remember you were free.
historical: The early church moved its day of worship to the first day, marking the resurrection, while keeping the principle that the body and soul need a rhythm of cessation. Augustine in the fourth century read the Sabbath as a sign of the eternal rest of God, and across the centuries the church has warned that a life without stopping is not strength but a quiet form of unbelief.
application: Choose a day, or even a steady block of hours, and stop, not to be more productive afterward but because you are commanded and loved. Put down the work, the screen, and the scorekeeping, and do the things that restore rather than consume you. Notice the guilt that rises when you rest, and name it, because it usually reveals exactly how much you have trusted your work instead of God. The world will keep turning. That is the point.

verses.text: On the seventh day God rested from all his work, and he blessed it and made it holy.
Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
There remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
Be still, and know that I am God.

articles.label: Practical guides for work and money

label: Success and Failure
framing: Scripture refuses both the worship of success and the despair of failure. It measures a life not by the heights it reaches but by the faithfulness it keeps, and it tells the story of God working through the failed, the overlooked, and the ones who had to start again. Your worst chapter is not your verdict.
cultural: The honor-shame world of the Bible kept a brutal ledger of public standing, where to fail was to be shamed before the whole community and to rise was everything. Into that, Jesus blessed the poor and the meek, chose fishermen over the famous, and built his kingdom on a cross, which Rome read as the ultimate failure, scrambling every scale the world used to keep score.
historical: The desert fathers fled the applause of the city precisely because they saw how success corrodes the soul. Augustine, in the fifth century, traced his climb up the ladder of worldly success and named it a long flight from God, and the church has ever since warned that the world's victories can ruin a person more surely than its defeats.
application: Hold your ambitions with an open hand, pursuing excellence without making it your god. When you fail, grieve it honestly, learn what it has to teach, and then receive the mercy that does not depend on your record. Refuse the endless comparison that measures your life against the highlight reel of another's. And remember that the call is not to be successful but to be faithful, and that the two are not the same.

verses.text: When I fall, I shall rise; when I sit in darkness, the Lord will be a light to me.
The righteous falls seven times and rises again.
My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.
What does it profit a man to gain the whole world and forfeit his soul.
Let us not grow weary of doing good, for in due season we will reap, if we do not give up.

articles.label: Practical guides for work and money

label: Justice and the Poor
framing: God's concern for the poor and the wronged is not a wing of the Bible. It runs through the whole of it, in the law, the prophets, the wisdom, and the words of Jesus. This is not a borrowed political cause. It is older than every modern party, and it judges all of them.
cultural: In the ancient world the widow, the orphan, and the foreigner had no household to protect them and no court that ruled in their favor, and so God wrote their protection directly into Israel's law, commanding gleaning, fair wages paid the same day, and courts that did not bend toward the powerful. The prophets later thundered against a worship that kept its feasts while the poor were crushed, calling it a thing God hated.
historical: The early church staggered Rome by feeding the hungry and burying the abandoned across every social line, and Basil of Caesarea built a city for the poor in the fourth century. From Chrysostom, who told the rich their surplus belonged to the poor, to Wilberforce against the slave trade, the church at its best has carried this ethic, and at its worst has betrayed it. The point is older than left and right, and it refuses to be owned by either.
application: Resist the reflex to sort this into a partisan box, because the moment you do, you let your party edit your Bible. The Scripture commands both personal generosity and just structures, both the open hand and the honest court, and a tribe that demands you choose only one half is asking you to obey it instead of God. Begin where you actually live: know a poor person by name, give real money, tell the truth in the rooms you are in, and let the prophets keep disturbing your comfort.

verses.text: Do justice, and love kindness, and walk humbly with your God.
Open your mouth for the mute, for the rights of all who are destitute.
Seek justice, correct oppression, bring justice to the fatherless, plead the widow's cause.
Let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.
Religion that is pure is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction.

articles.label: Practical guides for life in the world

label: Politics and Division
framing: The deepest line the Bible draws is not between left and right but between the kingdom of God and every kingdom that would claim your final loyalty. A faith captured by a political tribe has already traded its birthright. The danger is not that you hold convictions. It is that the tribe, not Christ, has become the thing you will not betray.
cultural: The first Christians lived under an empire that demanded ultimate allegiance and called Caesar lord, and they were killed for refusing that one word while paying their taxes and praying for their rulers. They confessed instead that Jesus is Lord, which relativized every earthly power without taking up its sword. They belonged to a kingdom that no party could contain and no emperor could co-opt.
historical: The church has been seduced by political power again and again, from the imperial bishops who blessed the throne, to the German churches that bent the knee to a regime in the 1930s, while Bonhoeffer and the Confessing Church paid for refusing to make the nation an idol. The lesson runs in every direction: when the church weds itself to a party, it loses both its prophetic voice and its soul.
application: Examine which voices form you most, and be honest if the talking heads of your side have discipled you more deeply than the Scriptures. Refuse contempt for the people across the line, since they too bear God's image and may sit beside you at the same table. Hold your political convictions firmly and your political tribe loosely, ready to be a thorn in your own side's flesh when it strays from Christ. And let no candidate, party, or cause receive the loyalty that belongs to God alone.

verses.text: Our citizenship is in heaven, and from it we await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ.
Put not your trust in princes, in a son of man, in whom there is no salvation.
Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's.
What causes quarrels and fights among you? Is it not your passions at war within you?
There is neither Jew nor Greek, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.

articles.label: Practical guides for life in the world

label: Technology and Distraction
framing: Your attention is not a small thing. It is the shape of your soul over time, since what you behold is what you become. The screen is not neutral, and a life given to endless scrolling is a life slowly trained to want what it sells. The question is not whether you use these tools, but who is forming whom.
cultural: Scripture knew nothing of phones, but it knew the war for the eyes and the heart, warning against the idols that promise life and deliver bondage, and against the restless craving that never says enough. The psalmist refused to set worthless things before his eyes, and Jesus called the eye the lamp of the whole body, knowing that what we gaze upon governs us.
historical: The desert fathers of the fourth century fled the noise of the city to learn attention and to fight the restless spirit they named acedia, the inability to be present. Augustine confessed his hunger to be entertained as a kind of slavery, and the long contemplative tradition has always taught that a scattered attention is a scattered self, and that the cure is silence, presence, and a fixed gaze on God.
application: Treat your attention as something worth guarding, because the people building these tools are spending billions to capture it. Put real friction between yourself and the reflex to reach for the phone, and reclaim the slow practices that train presence: Scripture read without a screen, prayer, a walk, a conversation no one is recording. Notice what the endless feed does to your contentment and your peace. And give your best attention, daily, to the One who made you to behold him.

verses.text: I will not set before my eyes anything that is worthless.
The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light.
Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth.
Whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is pure, think about these things.
Be still, and know that I am God.
